rule: Three colours form a network on a uniform background: many node blocks (filled squares), exactly two endpoint blocks (filled squares of a second colour) and strokes (8-connected components of a line colour). Blocks and strokes are pieces, and two pieces are adjacent if any of their cells touch, diagonals included. Find the shortest chain of pieces between the two endpoint blocks. Recolour the chain's strokes to 5 and its intermediate node blocks to 3. Endpoints, dead ends, longer alternative routes and disconnected parts stay unchanged.
scope: Construct separated square endpoint/node blocks and isolated 8-connected strokes; recolour the unique shortest endpoint chain, retaining dead ends and longer routes. Explicit fixture reconstruction uses the same unambiguous piece-graph contract.
constraints: Canonical validate fixtures exactly match; no fixture corrections.

authored_scope: Random scenes: grid sides are sampled independently from 12..30 (16/20..30 for 3x3 blocks or 2-thick strokes), or supplied. Blocks are uniformly 2x2 or 3x3, strokes are 1 or 2 thick, and 5..16 blocks are placed. The network is a spanning forest plus 0..3 cycle-closing links (about 70% of scenes have at least one) and 1..3 dead-end branches. Endpoints are chosen with a strictly unique shortest route of at least two links. When cycles exist, endpoints whose shortest route has a longer alternative are preferred about 75% of the time. Colours are 4 distinct values from {0,1,2,4,6,7,8,9}. Explicit scenes (used for fixture replay) accept arbitrary validated latent pieces and break ties the same way the reference BFS does. Deliberately not supported: random strokes that touch three or more blocks (branching strokes like some in the fixtures), mixed block sizes in random scenes, and tied shortest routes in random scenes.
authored_constraints: Four input colours are distinct and never 3 or 5; the background is strictly the most frequent colour (fewer than half the cells are non-background).
Blocks are separated by at least 2+thickness cells, so same-colour blocks never merge and blocks never touch each other.
Each random stroke touches exactly the blocks it links (one for a dead end, two for a link) and touches no other stroke, so latent pieces equal the painted 8-components.
At most one stroke links any pair of blocks; the shortest endpoint route in the block graph is strictly unique (path counting), so the chain is unambiguous.
The endpoints are at least two links apart, so at least one intermediate node becomes 3; at least one node block and one stroke stay off the chain.
The line colour has a non-square 4-component and there are at least 3 node blocks, so the reference role inference (block colours, then endpoint colour by count) is unambiguous.

Explicit scenes must have pieces that equal the painted components exactly: no overlaps, no touching same-colour blocks, no merged strokes and no empty strokes. Positive integer block sizes, at least 3 node blocks, a bent line component and a dominant background are required.
All loops are bounded: 600 placement tries, 8 tries per stroke, and 500 scene attempts, after which ValueError is raised. Infeasible size/density requests are rejected up front.
